chunks: # KERNELDARWIN ### Why is this GPU program slow? Keep the experiment that answers it. An evidence-first performance investigation laboratory. Profile a bounded workload, keep competing explanations, test targeted Triton configurations, and preserve the numerical checks and timing uncertainty behind

each decision. **v0.2.0 is a research preview.** The development host is an Apple M4, with no NVIDIA CUDA device. The release includes actual CPU control experiments, a fitted CPU intervention selector, and a prepared CUDA/Triton execution path. **No GPU speedup, GPU-trained policy, causal GPU diagnosis, sanitizer pass, or

GPU superiority is claimed.** [Validation status →](docs/validation.md) [Explore the LAB](https://nazeeh111.github.io/KERNELDARWIN/) · [Quickstart](#try-the-laboratory) · [Research](docs/research.md) · [Methodology](docs/methodology.md) · [Releases](https://github.com/nazeeh111/KERNELDARWIN/releases) ![Actual LAB overview with an explicitly labeled CPU control, paired latency distribution and verification ledger](docs/assets/v0.2/lab-desktop.png) ## One investigation, all the evidence The shipped controls compare a higher-precision NumPy reference with

batched float32-intermediate implementations within declared tolerances. They exercise the same record, correctness, paired timing, confirmation and learning components used by the CUDA path. They are **CPU software controls**, not evidence of GPU optimization. The reproducible suite contains **24 workloads, 72 attempted interventions, four operation families and six shapes**,

including strided inputs and no-improvement cases. Raw measurements, failed decisions, source identities and a trained model live in [the evidence directory](evidence/cpu-2026-10-26/). [Read the measured result and its limits](docs/results.md). The LAB now places the measured latency fingerprint and verification ledger together, with a keyboard-accessible timing-pair inspector, parent-aware candidate history,

and synchronized evidence selection. Its self-hosted IBM Plex typography and interruptible, reduced-motion-aware transitions serve the investigation. The LAB lets you follow the useful questions: what was measured, which explanation remains plausible, what changed, and what passed independent confirmation? GPU timelines, utilization and rooflines stay unavailable when their required

measurements are absent.

[Watch the current workbench recording](docs/assets/v0.2/workbench.mp4). The [original v0.1 demo](docs/demo/brag.mp4) is preserved. The current v0.2 workbench has a redesigned interface with paired-sample inspection, linked candidate selection, accessible lineage, and source comparison. CPU control playback remains labeled;

it is not live GPU optimization. ## Try the laboratory Python 3.11 or later. Basic installation has no runtime dependencies or model-provider credentials. ```bash git clone https://github.com/nazeeh111/KERNELDARWIN.git cd KERNELDARWIN python -m pip install . kd doctor kd lab # Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 ``` The public LAB is static and

reads recorded JSON. It never compiles or executes uploaded code. Import a record or inspect the bundled controls. No public GPU execution service is exposed. For actual local CPU controls: ```bash python -m pip install '.[control]' kd control --family softmax --shape 128 1024 --store .runs kd train --store

evidence/cpu-2026-10-26/records --device-kind cpu --output .runs/cpu-model.json python -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` CPU models cannot be used to choose CUDA interventions. [CLI and Python API →](docs/usage.md) ## Run the CUDA path **Requires Linux, an NVIDIA GPU with compute capability 8.0 or newer, a compatible driver, PyTorch and

Triton. This path has not been executed on the release host.** Optional dependencies are version-bounded; inspect `kd doctor` and your platform's PyTorch installation requirements. ```bash python -m pip install '.[cuda]' kd doctor kd investigate --family softmax --shape 128 1024 --max-candidates 6 --trace --store .runs kd validate .runs/RECORD_ID.json #

Export only after correctness + discovery + independent confirmation pass: kd export .runs/RECORD_ID.json --output optimized.py ``` The authored templates cover these finite-input, two-dimensional workloads: | Family | Declared semantics | Initial configuration search | |---|---|---| | `sum` | Last-dimension reduction | Row block size and warp count |

| `softmax` | Stable row softmax | Row block size and warp count | | `layernorm` | Row normalization, population variance, configurable epsilon, no affine parameters | Row block size and warp count | | `fused` | `relu(float32(x) * 1.5 + 0.25)`, cast to input dtype | Element

tile size and warp count | Supported dtypes: float32, float16, bfloat16. Positive strides, nonempty shapes, at most 8,192 columns. No autograd/backward contract, arbitrary CUDA source, matmul optimizer or whole-model replacement is claimed. These are inference adapters. The exported callable enforces the verified shape, dtype, strides, device and source

identity. GPU timing uses warmup, synchronization, randomized paired baseline/candidate ordering, and repeated CUDA events. Compilation/first dispatch is reported separately. Promotion requires reference correctness, a bootstrap lower speedup bound above 1.03, then a fresh-input confirmation. `torch.compile` is measured separately when available. Memory safety remains unverified until independently checked with

the supported [sanitizer procedure](docs/usage.md#memory-safety-and-profiling). A constrained subprocess runs only finite authored templates, with a timeout and an environment allowlist; it is not a hostile-code sandbox. [An attention application benchmark](examples/attention.py) integrates an exported softmax into `QKᵀ → softmax → V` and compares eager, compiled and optimized application paths. It

requires a real accepted CUDA export. **No application-level GPU result has been collected.** ## From hypothesis to intervention ![Implemented experiment workflow and future causal evidence boundary](docs/assets/workflow.svg) The current selector is a compact contextual ridge model with an uncertainty bonus. It learns from recorded rewards, failure outcomes and experiment

costs. Offline evaluation holds out whole families and shapes, compares random selection, fixed rules and sequential Gaussian-process Bayesian selection, and ablates workload context and uncertainty. CPU replay results do not establish the GPU research question. Standard Triton autotuning and existing agent baselines still require an actual matched CUDA

study. Hypotheses preserve evidence, missing measurements and falsifiers. The preview does not update them into proven causes merely because one candidate is faster. Diagnosis-conditioned learning, profiler-feature ablations and hardware holdouts remain research work. [Prior art and licensing →](docs/prior-art.md) ## Build on it - [Install, CLI/API, export and troubleshooting](docs/usage.md)

- [Benchmark credibility and semantic contracts](docs/methodology.md) - [Research question, comparisons and limits](docs/research.md) - [Selector features, training and evaluation](docs/selector.md) - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) and [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [License and attribution](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), [citation](CITATION.cff), [release notes](CHANGELOG.md) CPU CI validates contracts and distributions. GPU validation is a manual workflow requiring an explicitly provisioned trusted self-hosted runner;

this project supplies no paid compute. Open an issue with a reproducible record, workload specification and environment when reporting a problem. Do not include private data or credentials. Apache-2.0 · Copyright 2026 Nazeeh Abdul-Hadi

# Architecture The Python core has no required runtime dependencies. Optional backends import only when selected. | Component | Responsibility | |---|---| | `records.py` | Typed workload/configuration contracts, validation and atomic immutable JSON storage | | `statistics.py` | Latency summaries and paired-bootstrap promotion gate | | `hypotheses.py` |

Analytical diagnostic leads, missing evidence and falsifiers | | `selector.py` | Small ridge/UCB model, saved weights, grouped replay and baselines | | `control.py` | Actual NumPy CPU experiments for validating software behavior | | `kernels.py`, `gpu.py` | Bounded authored Triton templates, PyTorch references, correctness checks, CUDA timing and

trace extraction | | `engine.py` | Candidate budget, failed attempts, fresh-input confirmation, worker subprocess | | `cli.py` | Explicit backend selection, record inspection, training, export and read-only LAB | | `lab/` | Static, dependency-free evidence viewer, also included in the wheel | The public viewer has no compute

backend. A user imports JSON locally; source strings are rendered as text. Local `kd investigate` invokes only predefined templates through a worker with an environment allowlist and a hard timeout. This limits accidental resource use; it is not a security sandbox for arbitrary generated programs. No LLM API,

service account, database or message bus is needed. Raw records are the stable handoff between CLI, learning and UI. A record's self-reported provenance and structural validation are not cryptographic proof of execution. Promotion validation recomputes gates from raw timings, while execution authenticity still requires inspecting collection logs and

the source/environment. Changes in kernel source invalidate export of an earlier candidate. Kernel source/semantic correctness, numerical tolerances and measured performance are different checks. The current hypothesis engine offers test plans without claiming causal inference. A future controlled experiment layer can attach counter evidence and interventions to these IDs

# Investigation workbench v0.2 The interface starts with the measured workload, not a marketing headline. A charcoal instrument field, chalk type, steel reference trace, restrained orange candidate signal, and pale verification green connect the brand to its scientific task. The original branching K mark remains. Self-hosted IBM Plex

Sans and Mono make typography consistent without remote font calls. ## Reading order A compact record bar selects the investigation and states the evidence type. The overview pairs the latency fingerprint with its verification ledger; both follow the selected candidate. The distribution and paired-sample modes use actual recorded

observations. An accessible range input inspects a specific pair. Reference/candidate medians, quantiles and the reported confidence interval use the same measurement phase. Tiny nonzero errors use scientific notation. The intervention table preserves failed attempts. Flat search histories use a continuous baseline-to-attempt bus with a single horizontally scrollable row

for larger pools. Branched, cyclic or unresolved histories are grouped by their actual parent IDs, with no fabricated graph edges. Implementation panels show original text and unique-line highlighting, explicitly distinguished from a semantic diff. Atlas and research controls retain actual record filtering and held-out budgets. ## Code and

motion `lab/app.js` owns state and navigation. `lab/js/records.js` validates incoming records, `model.js` contains pure numerical/data transforms, `charts.js` draws actual measurements, `lineage.js` preserves parent identity, `overview.js`/`inspection.js` render views, `dom.js` constructs text-safe DOM, and `motion.js` owns interruptible Web Animations. No runtime framework or animation dependency is required. Navigation changes use a

short opacity/position transition while the shell stays stable. Candidate changes reveal the affected evidence. Repeated input cancels prior motion; reduced motion resolves immediately, including preference changes. Values never count up from invented intermediate measurements. No idle pulse implies a live GPU. ## Trust and accessibility CPU controls, references

and CUDA records remain separate. The viewer checks consistency; `kd validate` independently recomputes statistical gates. A bad import cannot replace a valid record or poison another view. Missing profiler evidence stays absent. Large traces use bounded extrema computation and disclose their 300-visible-event cap. No imported code executes. All

icon-only navigation retains accessible names. Native selects, buttons, disclosures and range controls preserve keyboard behavior. Focus survives candidate/record changes. Responsive layouts retain the same content across phone, tablet and desktop. CSS and Web Animations honor reduced motion. Current-source checks and the exact tested scope are recorded in `assets/v0.2/qa.json`;

passing checks do not claim universal accessibility conformance. ## Reproduce The Python package includes every module, font and license. `kd lab` serves it read-only. For source work, `python3 -m http.server 8766 --directory lab` is sufficient. `npm test` runs dependency-free frontend unit tests. Optional browser tests: `npm ci`, `npx
playwright install chromium`, `npm run test:browser`. A native Chrome path can be supplied with `PW_EXECUTABLE_PATH` for a local isolated test profile. Browser test dependencies are development-only.

# Figure provenance `assets/workflow.svg` and `assets/cpu-selection.svg` are original editable vector figures. Regenerate with `python scripts/render_figures.py`. Workflow elements map to `gpu.py` profiling/reference adapters, `hypotheses.py` diagnostic leads, `engine.py` candidate scheduling/confirmation, `statistics.py` bootstrap checks and `selector.py` offline replay. The explicit research-open line prevents an implemented stage diagram from implying validated causal

or GPU learning outcomes. The loop denotes retained experiment feedback; online causal-confidence updating is not implemented. Numerical bars come from `evidence/cpu-2026-10-26/cpu-selector.evaluation.json`, family split, candidate budget 1. They show mean best discovery log-speedup, not aggregate final GPU speedup. The title states the negative comparison against the fixed heuristic. SVG

IDs preserve panel/bar editability. PaperVizAgent was investigated and credited in prior art. Its model-service configuration is unnecessary for these deterministic diagrams and would conflict with the no-billed-API constraint. No PaperVizAgent-generated output or code is included.

# Measurement and verification protocol This document defines how to interpret an investigation and what is required before accepting a performance claim. It includes follow-up research requirements beyond the bounded preview implementation. A field marked unavailable or not run is a limit, not a pass. Read the record

and current source alongside this protocol. ## Record the contract first Record operation semantics, full shape, strides, dtype, epsilon where relevant, seed, input-generation method, source/configuration identity, device model/architecture and software versions. Preserve compiler settings and timing mode. Capture driver/runtime, clocks, power and concurrent activity where observable; explicitly list

unavailable conditions. Do not silently substitute CPU execution for a requested CUDA run. Keep PyTorch eager as the declared CUDA reference. Measure `torch.compile` separately if it succeeds, retaining any failure reason. Separate first-call compilation/setup from steady-state latency. A template candidate has the same output shape, dtype and declared

numerical semantics as its reference. Unsupported shapes and layouts fail clearly rather than falling back invisibly. ## Correctness precedes speed Use independent fresh inputs across seeds, zeros, constants, negative values, small and large finite values, odd sizes, boundary widths, supported noncontiguous strides and each declared dtype. Compare against

the reference with recorded absolute and relative tolerances appropriate to the dtype and operation. Report maximum error and case count; any mismatched case invalidates that candidate. A first numerical suite is not proof over all inputs. Specifically test that changed inputs change outputs as expected, previous inputs are

not cached as results, output storage is fresh where promised, and input tensors remain unmodified. Keep the tested source/configuration identity with the result. Never accept a precision change, missing computation, stale output or hidden CPU fallback as an optimization. NaN/Inf semantics need a declared contract and tests before

support is claimed. Compute Sanitizer is a separate diagnostic route on supported CUDA installations. Run `memcheck` before relying on `racecheck`; synchronization and initialization checks cover other failure classes. [NVIDIA documents](https://docs.nvidia.com/compute-sanitizer/ComputeSanitizer/) that shared-memory race detection is not general memory checking. Preserve exact invocation, exit code and logs. A missing

tool must remain `not_run` or unavailable. ## Timing Warm the exact callable and synchronize as required. Collect repeated GPU measurements using CUDA events for device work, keeping measurement setup and synchronization consistent. Interleave baseline and candidate measurements with randomized order within each pair to reduce drift bias. Store

raw per-pair microseconds and the order/seed; do not retain only a rounded headline. Use normal launches as the default timing mode. CUDA graph replay is a distinct mode and must be labeled and compared like for like. Host wall-time or application timing answers a different question from isolated

device-event timing. Count dispatch, transfers, allocations or graph capture only where the declared benchmark includes them. Retain compile/setup cost separately. Summarize median, spread, number of observations and coefficient of variation. The preview's paired bootstrap reports a 95% interval for the ratio of baseline and candidate medians; it resamples

complete pairs. The basic acceptance threshold requires at least 20 pairs and an interval lower bound exceeding the configured minimum speedup, normally 1.03. This is a practical noise gate, not an automatic guarantee of an unbiased experiment or a universal significance test. Searching many candidates creates selection bias.

After selecting a winner, independently rerun that source/configuration with new timing samples and correctness inputs. For a headline, reproduce in a fresh process/session and report failures and variability. Where candidates are nearly tied, preserve the simpler or established implementation rather than overstating a fractional gain. Never aggregate unrelated

tasks as though repeated samples were additional workloads. ## Diagnosis and counters Collect counters separately from fair latency timing. [Nsight Compute](https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/) may replay kernels/applications, control clocks and alter cache conditions; the report must state those settings. A trace establishes recorded events, not an inferred hardware utilization percentage. In

the absence of actual counter/trace data, the LAB must show that absence. Use controlled interventions to distinguish explanations. Change one relevant factor at a time where practical. Separate observed speedup from a hypothesized mechanism. Keep failed experiments and unresolved alternatives. Analytical bandwidth or arithmetic-intensity calculations must expose assumptions

and byte/FLOP accounting. Do not fabricate hardware ceilings or claim a roofline bottleneck without suitable evidence. ## Budget, isolation and integration Specify maximum candidates, timeout and workload-size limits before the run. Record invalid candidates and timeouts as costs. Run only bounded trusted templates in the preview; imported JSON

is data and never executable code. A subprocess timeout and sanitized environment reduce operational risk but are not a security sandbox. Arbitrary generated GPU programs require a separately provisioned worker/container with enforced resource limits, restricted mounts and no credentials or unnecessary network. An exported accepted kernel must be

callable from a supported application and enforce its supported input contract. Reproduce the result in that integration and measure the complete application path against eager/compiled alternatives. Microbenchmark speedup does not imply application speedup. Preserve the unoptimized implementation as a fallback where contract support is narrower. ## Reproduction package

Retain versioned raw records, source/configuration, seeds, paired samples, numerical results, failures, timing mode and environment information. Separate `cpu_control`, actual CUDA measurements and external/reference records. Include training/test group identities and policy parameters with learned-selection reports. No CPU or replay result may be relabeled as a new CUDA run. The

development host for this preview is Apple M4/macOS. It cannot establish CUDA correctness, CUDA-event performance, NVIDIA counter observations or Compute Sanitizer outcomes. Those validations must be completed on compatible Linux/NVIDIA hardware before GPU success is claimed.

# Research report: diagnosis before intervention **Research preview. No CUDA performance claim is established by this release's development host.** The Apple M4 host cannot execute this project's NVIDIA CUDA path. CPU controls and tests establish software behavior in their stated scope. They do not establish a GPU speedup,

a GPU-trained policy, a causal GPU diagnosis, or cross-device generalization. ## Question and intended contribution Can an explicit performance-hypothesis ledger help select useful interventions using fewer expensive GPU experiments than random search, fixed heuristics, standard Triton autotuning or Bayesian optimization? The proposed contribution is the connection between three

artifacts: a falsifiable explanation, an intervention chosen to test it, and a reproducible correctness/performance decision. Each experiment should make a diagnosis more useful, not merely find another fast parameter value. A successful research result would show that this connection improves decisions under a fixed budget on held-out tasks.

This is an empirical question, not a novelty or superiority claim. Profiling, kernel generation, learned cost models, counter-guided search and graphical search histories all have strong precedents. [The prior-art review](prior-art.md) identifies these overlaps. The preview uses bounded kernel templates so that algorithm changes, precision changes and search strategy

can be assessed separately. It does not promise arbitrary-program optimization. ## Competing mechanisms Three practical routes were considered: | Route | Mechanism | Decisive limitation or test | |---|---|---| | Profile-guided free-form agent search | Use model reasoning and compiler/runtime feedback to generate new programs. | Larger semantic

and isolation burden; already demonstrated by prior systems. A model-provider dependency is unnecessary for the first evidence loop. | | Exhaustive or Bayesian template search | Search a known configuration space and verify each candidate. | Strong conventional route. It may match a learned selector on this small

space; compare equal budgets and include fitting overhead. | | Evidence-conditioned intervention selection | Learn which controlled tests are informative/useful for a workload, preserving rejected explanations and failures. | Chosen research direction. It succeeds only if evidence improves held-out selection beyond ordinary workload/configuration features. | The simplest useful

first model is regularized linear regression with an uncertainty bonus for unexplored contexts. Regularization discourages unstable coefficients when data are sparse. An upper-confidence score balances predicted value and exploration; it is a ranking heuristic, not a calibrated probability that a bottleneck is causal. This is easier to audit

and ablate than a large reinforcement-learning system. The exact implemented features and serialization are described in [selector documentation](selector.md). ## Experimental unit and evidence A task is a complete workload specification, hardware/software environment and reference semantic contract. A candidate is a distinct kernel configuration or named implementation intervention. Observations

must preserve task identity, source/configuration identity, valid/invalid outcome, paired timing samples, numerical checks and experiment cost. Invalid candidates consume budget and remain in the history. A diagnosis entry includes supporting observations, unavailable measurements, an experiment and a falsifier. For example, a launch-overhead explanation should be tested using a

size sweep or an explicit launch/graph intervention while holding semantics and timing mode fixed. A memory-bandwidth explanation needs measured traffic/bandwidth evidence or a documented analytical bound plus a controlled access-pattern intervention. A faster configuration alone cannot establish register pressure or occupancy as the cause. The preview's heuristic explanations

are candidate explanations. Unless a controlled experiment distinguishes alternatives, preserve them as unconfirmed. Confidence labels are evidence summaries, not trained causal probabilities. Roofline plots require defensible FLOP/byte counts and appropriate device ceilings; unavailable quantities remain absent rather than being guessed. ## Evaluation plan and current limits The table

separates planned comparisons from the software's offline evaluation. An evaluation function existing in source does not mean that a scientifically meaningful GPU dataset has been evaluated. | Comparison | Controlled requirement | CUDA evidence in this preview | |---|---|---| | Random selection | Same candidate pool, many fixed

seeds, equal measured budget | Not collected on the development host | | Rule-based heuristic | Frozen rules before test collection; equal pool and budget | Not collected on the development host | | Learned ranking and uncertainty ablation | Train only on designated training groups; freeze model

before test | GPU-trained evaluation pending | | Profiling-evidence ablation | Same model/features except measured evidence; no post-outcome leakage | Pending measured counters and intervention data | | Hypothesis-testing ablation | Same candidates/budget with diagnosis-conditioned scheduling disabled | Pending a matched controlled study | | Standard Triton autotuning

| Invoke its real tuning path using equivalent configs and timing semantics | Pending CUDA execution | | Bayesian optimization | Same domain/budget, count fit cost | Implemented sequential RBF GP-UCB CPU replay; actual CUDA/BoTorch comparison pending | | Existing agent optimization | Pin system, model/provider, tokens, hardware

and spend; preserve failures | Not reproduced; no paid model/compute is assumed | Split by whole task groups. Hold out operation families to assess transfer, unseen shape regimes within known families to assess shape generalization, and whole hardware configurations when multiple GPUs exist. All observations of a task,

including repeats and failed variants, stay in the same fold. Hardware holdout requires more than one hardware configuration; otherwise report it unavailable. Choose hyperparameters using training/validation groups only. For each test task, report best independently verified latency after each experiment budget, experiments and wall time to first accepted

improvement, invalid fraction, regret relative to the measured candidate pool, and diagnostic evidence coverage. Aggregate tasks with task-level uncertainty; repeated timing samples are not independent workloads. Include both no-improvement cases and losses. Count data-collection, compilation, fitting and profiling costs separately. Do not train on the test-task outcome and

call the resulting replay prospective performance. The shipped grouped replay is a software-level evaluator on recorded observations. It does not reconstruct temporal hardware noise, guarantee causal effects, or substitute for a prospective optimizer run. CPU controls can reveal bugs and exercise training/evaluation. External historical CUDA data, such as

the CC BY 4.0 KTT dataset, could support a separately attributed replay study, but its operations, hardware and candidate semantics differ from the initial Triton scope. That route has not been adopted as current-device validation. The official dataset page and anonymous folder metadata were accessible during review, but

a subsequent raw-file metadata request returned HTTP 403. No dataset bytes, model or historical training results are bundled from that route. ## Conditions for a publishable result Freeze the workload suite and budgets, collect a training corpus on real NVIDIA hardware, then measure held-out results independently. Verify accepted

candidates on new seeds and relevant boundary/stride/dtype cases, rerun paired performance confirmation, and run supported sanitizer tools. Measure one integrated application path, including dispatch costs, rather than only isolated kernels. Publish raw records and exact environment/source identities. If diagnosis-conditioned selection does not beat simpler baselines, report the null

result. The investigation record, failure archive and reproducible verification workflow remain useful without a positive ML result. A single fast kernel, a passing CPU suite, or an attractive interface is insufficient evidence for the research hypothesis.

# Measured CPU controls and the null selection result The release contains actual NumPy CPU measurements on an Apple M4 arm64 development host, using Python 3.12.14 and NumPy as recorded per run. There was no NVIDIA GPU execution. These controls validate the implementation and evidence pipeline; they do

not answer the GPU research question. The suite has 24 workloads: sum, softmax, layernorm and fused elementwise across shapes (32,31), (128,257), (128,1024), (256,513), (512,2048), (96,4095). The (256,513) cases use last-dimension stride 2. Every workload tests three actual NumPy batch sizes: 32, 128 and 512 rows. `num_warps=1` is an

unused schema placeholder in CPU controls, not a GPU configuration result. Each implementation is independently compared with a float64-intermediate reference cast to the input dtype, using the stated numerical tolerances. Candidates use float32 intermediates. This declared reference distinction is one reason the CPU timings must not be marketed

as GPU improvements. After warmup, each candidate receives 40 paired, randomly ordered timings. One selected candidate receives a separate fresh-input confirmation. The suite retains 20 accepted CPU-control results and four no-improvement cases. Raw samples and all candidates are in [records](../evidence/cpu-2026-10-26/records/); accepted status concerns only these CPU semantics and

# Evidence-backed resume bullets - Built KERNELDARWIN, a Python/Triton performance-investigation research preview with immutable experiment records, independent numerical checks, paired-bootstrap timing gates and a static eight-view evidence workbench; CUDA hardware validation remains pending. - Trained and evaluated a compact intervention-ranking model on 72 measured CPU interventions across four

operation families and six shapes, with family/shape holdouts, Bayesian/random/rule baselines and ablations; reported that learned selection matched the simple heuristic rather than claiming an unmeasured GPU advantage.

# Intervention selection KERNELDARWIN uses an explicit small ridge regression model with an upper-confidence-style acquisition score. No pretrained model is shipped. `fit()` learns real-valued weights from supplied, recorded observations; JSON inputs are evidence claims and cannot independently attest hardware execution. Each observation contains `workload`, `candidate`, `reward`, `cost`, `valid`,

`group` (source run identifier), and `device_kind` (`cpu` or `cuda`). Recommended reward is natural log of measured baseline/candidate median latency. Cost is measured experiment wall time in seconds. Invalid candidates have an explicit penalty. Utility is `reward - 1*(not valid) - .02*log1p(cost)`. Changing the units changes this penalty, so

datasets must use one cost unit consistently. The versioned feature vector includes log-scaled row count, row width, stride, dtype, four operation-family indicators, tile/batch size, warp count, and configuration interactions. CPU controls use block size as row batch size and one warp as a schema placeholder; this is not

GPU tuning. The model fits `A = XᵀX + λI`, `θ = A⁻¹Xᵀy`, with pivoted elimination in the standard library. Ranking uses `θᵀx + α√(xᵀA⁻¹x)`; defaults are λ=1, α=.25. The latter term measures feature leverage, not a calibrated confidence interval. No automatic claim of Bayesian posterior validity is

made. ```python from kerneldarwin.selector import InterventionSelector, evaluate_grouped model = InterventionSelector().fit(observations) ranked = model.rank({**spec.to_dict(), "device_kind": "cpu"}, candidates) model.save("selector.json") report = evaluate_grouped(observations, seed=0) ``` A model refuses mixed CPU/CUDA training and rejects explicit device-kind mismatch at ranking. Pass `device_kind` when ranking. Persisted models include feature version, weights, regularized design matrix,

observation count, device domain, and source group identifiers. ## What evaluation establishes `evaluate_grouped` replays a finite, observed candidate table using leave-one-family-out and leave-one-shape-out folds. Seeds for the same workload stay together. Each fold trains only on other families/shapes, then ranks that fold's observed interventions. It reports best measured

reward and total measured cost within each candidate-count budget, and oracle gap. Repeated observations of the same intervention are averaged inside a holdout workload. There is no imputation of missing candidate outcomes. Comparisons include 32 seeded random permutations per workload, a declared batching/warp heuristic, the learned selector, a

no-context ablation (configuration features only), a no-uncertainty ablation, and a sequential finite-pool Gaussian-process upper-confidence-bound (GP-UCB) Bayesian-optimization baseline. The CPU heuristic tries the largest row batch first. The GPU heuristic tries warp counts nearest four for rows up to 4096 columns and eight above that threshold. These simple heuristics

are declared baselines, not asserted best practice. The learned policies use offline initial rankings. The GP-UCB baseline updates its posterior after every selected candidate outcome. This is not an online bandit regret proof, a calibrated uncertainty study, a causal bottleneck detector, standard Triton autotuning, a BoTorch execution, or

a replication of KernelAgent/Kernel Forge. It neither trains nor validates cross-device transfer. Genuine CUDA observations and hardware holdouts remain necessary for the GPU research question. CPU controls validate learning, serialization and evaluation plumbing only. Negative results must remain in the report. ## Bayesian baseline and information boundaries `bayesian_order(candidates,

observe, seed=0)` implements a compact, sequential GP-UCB baseline using only the standard library. It starts from one seeded random configuration. After selecting a candidate, it calls `observe(candidate)` to reveal that candidate's recorded reward. It fits a zero-mean, unit-variance Gaussian process with an RBF covariance kernel over `log2(block_size)/16` and

`log2(num_warps)/5`, then chooses the remaining candidate maximizing posterior mean plus twice posterior standard deviation. The kernel length scale is fixed at .25; observation noise variance is fixed at 1e-4. The posterior is solved directly with the same pivoted small-system solver used by the selector. Hyperparameters are declared in

advance and are not fitted on held-out outcomes. Grouped replay runs 32 seeded initializations per workload and averages best reward and measured cost at each candidate-count budget, matching the number of seeded random permutations. Unselected rewards are hidden from each sequential GP policy until selection; the complete recorded

table is used by the evaluator afterward to score each prefix and the oracle gap. The GP learns within a workload, while the contextual selector learns across training workloads. Their different information paths are part of the comparison and are retained in the report. This baseline does not
invoke BoTorch, reproduce all practical Bayesian-optimization choices, estimate heteroscedastic timing noise, or launch additional CPU/GPU work. CPU replay remains CPU-only evidence.

# Installation and use Basic: Python >=3.11, `python -m pip install .`. CPU controls add `.[control]`; CUDA adds `.[cuda]`. Supported CUDA scope is Linux and NVIDIA compute capability >=8.0 with compatible drivers. `kd doctor` reports availability, optional profiler tools and exact requirements. CPU CI does not install CUDA.

## CLI ```bash kd --help kd doctor kd control --family layernorm --shape 256 513 --stride 2 --seed 42 --store .runs kd investigate --family softmax --shape 128 1024 --dtype float32 --max-candidates 6 --repeats 40 --wall-seconds 180 --trace --store .runs kd show .runs/ID.json kd validate .runs/ID.json kd train --store .runs

--device-kind cuda --output .runs-models/cuda-policy.json kd investigate --family softmax --shape 128 1024 --model .runs-models/cuda-policy.json kd regress before.json after.json kd export .runs/ID.json --output optimized.py kd lab ``` `investigate` returns exit 2 and saves a blocked reference record if CUDA or Triton is unavailable. Invalid configuration/failed execution returns 1. A completed

investigation with no improvement returns 0 and preserves all attempts. Each record is a new file. Existing record IDs are never overwritten. `train` requires at least 12 observations across two families. Keep models/evaluations outside the run store: it contains investigation records only. CPU and CUDA observations cannot be

mixed, and a CPU-trained policy cannot rank a CUDA investigation. GPU hardware transfer is not validated. The current model uses shape/family/layout/configuration features, not measured profiler features. Invalid attempted candidates are retained with a failure penalty and no invented speedup. `regress` compares two compatible recorded baselines using an independent

bootstrap interval. It checks workload, stable device identity and software environment; differences in observed device telemetry are reported. The comparison detects a repeatable difference in those records, not its cause. To investigate a revision slowdown, collect controlled runs of each implementation, inspect source/trace/layout changes, then test the targeted

repair. Automatic Git bisection is not implemented. The prepared engine invokes authored templates, not arbitrary revisions. ## Python API ```python from pathlib import Path from kerneldarwin.records import WorkloadSpec, ExperimentStore from kerneldarwin.engine import investigate_cuda, observation_rows from kerneldarwin.selector import InterventionSelector spec = WorkloadSpec(family="softmax", shape=(128, 1024), dtype="float32") # CUDA required; direct

API uses the calling process. Prefer CLI for timeout. record = investigate_cuda(spec, max_candidates=6, repeats=40) path = ExperimentStore(Path(".runs")).save(record) observations = observation_rows(ExperimentStore(".runs").list()) model = InterventionSelector().fit(observations) ranking = model.rank({**spec.to_dict(), "device_kind": "cuda"}, [ {"block_size": 1024, "num_warps": 4}, {"block_size": 1024, "num_warps": 8}, ]) ``` `gpu.reference(family,x,eps)` is the declared PyTorch reference; `gpu.candidate(family,config,x,eps)` is the

authored Triton adapter. They are inference functions with finite-input semantics; no autograd contract. CPU-only imports work without PyTorch or Triton. ## Integrate an accepted export `kd export` accepts only a CUDA record whose winner passed discovery and fresh numerical/timing confirmation. It checks current kernel source identity. The exported

callable rechecks source identity and input/device/stride contracts when invoked. It requires the installed matching KERNELDARWIN CUDA package; it is not a vendored independent Triton distribution. ```python from optimized import run output = run(cuda_input) ``` Run `python examples/attention.py optimized.py --output application.json` after exporting a contiguous softmax record. It measures

attention's `QKᵀ / sqrt(d) → softmax → V` path with eager, optimized and compiled baselines. No application result is bundled until actual CUDA execution. Shape-specific microkernel gains do not imply end-to-end gains. ## Memory safety and profiling Run numerical checks separately from timing: ```bash python scripts/sanitizer_check.py compute-sanitizer --tool

memcheck --error-exitcode 86 python scripts/sanitizer_check.py compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck --error-exitcode 86 python scripts/sanitizer_check.py compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck --error-exitcode 86 python scripts/sanitizer_check.py ``` Inspect exit codes and logs. Racecheck targets shared-memory hazards; it does not prove all memory accesses safe. Sanitizer results are not automatically attached or marked passed in run

records. The script checks the authored configurations at a bounded shape; it does not prove safety for every possible input. `--trace` captures a separate PyTorch profiler pass and extracts real CUDA duration events. The raw Chrome trace is stored under `STORE/traces/`; traces do not train the selector. Trace

overhead is excluded from benchmark samples. A missing profiler/CUPTI path records unavailable evidence. Optional Nsight Compute counters should be collected in a separate profiler pass and interpreted with their units and replay settings. Automatic Nsight/Proton integration is not implemented in this preview. The LAB deliberately omits rooflines/utilization when

required measurements are absent. The manual GitHub GPU workflow requires a trusted self-hosted Linux CUDA runner that you explicitly provision. It never triggers on incoming pull requests. No paid runner or cloud service is provisioned. ## Reproduce CPU evidence ```bash python -m pip install '.[control]' python scripts/control_suite.py --output

evidence/my-new-run kd train --store evidence/my-new-run/records --device-kind cpu --output evidence/my-new-run/cpu-model.json python scripts/check_evidence.py ``` The suite uses 40 paired measurements after warmup, 4 families × 6 shapes × 3 row-batch interventions. NumPy uses float32 candidates against a higher-precision reference and declared tolerances. These results test the software, not GPU search

quality. `control_suite.py` refuses to reuse a destination; preserve earlier measurements. ## Troubleshooting - **No CUDA / Apple Silicon:** use the LAB and CPU controls. Metal does not validate NVIDIA code. Do not relabel CPU runs as CUDA. - **Triton compilation fails:** preserve the error and software/device versions. The

path has not been compiler-tested on the release host. No speedup is accepted from a failed candidate. - **No candidate accepted:** this is a valid result. Inspect correctness, noise and confirmation before increasing the budget. - **Existing export path:** choose a new filename; exports never silently overwrite an

existing file. - **Source mismatch:** rerun the investigation with current code; never transplant old acceptance metadata onto changed source. - **LAB has no bundled records:** serve over HTTP with `kd lab`; local-file fetch restrictions vary. Local import still reads JSON as data. Run `kd validate` to independently re-evaluate
record consistency and timing gates. - **Missing model/service API key:** none is required. No billed model provider is used.
